newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares fall amid summer lull.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares fall amid summer lull.

text.p: Norwegian shares traded in negative territory on Tuesday on slow turnover with many investors, both domestic and foreign, being away on holiday.

"Its holiday time," a dealer said. "Not only are Norwegian investors off, but foreign investors are gone now too. We had a lot of orders from London-based clients in July, but they are now off on holiday."
"A quiet day," another said. "Some big clients, especially Americans, are waiting for U.S. economic indicators to be released this week."
Turnover was low at 617 million crowns.
Oslo's Total share index, which rallied last week bouyed by a strong dollar, closed 0.44 percent lower at 1,264.50 points.

Industrial conglomerate Norsk Hydro fell 1.5 percent, or six crowns, to 387 crowns on profit-taking and falling urea prices, a dealer said. It was the most traded share at 75 million crowns. Ocean Rig, at 65 million crowns, was the second most traded share for the third consecutive session. After rising 14 percent since Friday on speculation of a new contract, the share fell 2.3 percent, or 0.40 crowns, to 16.70 crowns in what appeared to be a correction.
